content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves D5 vs C5 by using individual chapter-bound verses and an almah/bethulah word-count to declare the link underdetermined, so it does the verse-level weighing K-C governs when a pressing side's own chain is read together.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse — I weighed whether the judge's use of chapter bounds and word-count is prohibited verse-by-verse weighing versus a legitimate chain-by-footing summary.","why":"K-C requires chain-against-chain by footing and forbids verse-by-verse deciding, but the judge text balances chapter bounds and word-count instead of chain footings."}
